item.title: Starbucks pilots AI‑driven personalized drive‑thru menus
item.description:
Starbucks pilots AI‑driven personalized drive‑thru menus

Starbucks announced that it will experiment with artificial‑intelligence tools to recognize customers as they arrive at its drive‑thrus and serve each car a personalized digital menu.

🔍 Overview

  • The company plans to “recognize participating customers as they arrive, present personalized digital menus, and make payment more effortless” (CEO Brian Niccol, earnings call).
  • The effort is described as an early‑stage experiment that will be tested, learned from, and scaled if successful.

🛠️ How it works

  • Customer recognition – AI will identify a car or its occupants when they pull up to the lane.
  • Personalized menu display – A digital board will show menu items tailored to the recognized customer.
  • Background order‑entry AI (2027) – Starting in 2027, AI models will assist baristas in entering orders more accurately and efficiently.
  • App integration – AI will be added to the Starbucks app’s search and discovery features, with future support for “conversational and agentic” ordering.
  • Existing AI tools – Customers can already place orders through ChatGPT, and employees use the AI‑powered Green Dot Assist for recipe and service‑standard queries.

📋 Features

  • Recognize customers at the drive‑thru entrance.
  • Show a personalized digital menu per car.
  • Streamline payment and order entry.
  • Test background AI models for barista assistance beginning in 2027.
  • Expand AI to app search, discovery, and conversational ordering.
  • Existing ChatGPT ordering channel and employee‑focused Green Dot Assist.

📊 Comparison with peers

Company AI Drive‑Thru Feature Personalization Detail
Starbucks Recognize customers, display personalized digital menu, background order‑entry AI (2027) Car‑by‑car menu customization based on identified customer
Taco Bell Experiments with menu boards that change layout, content, visuals on a car‑by‑car basis Similar car‑specific visual changes
McDonald’s “ArchIQ” chatbot identifies repeat customers and lets them order their “usual” Repeat‑customer ordering via chatbot

🚀 Timeline / Availability

  • Now – Announcement and early testing phase (CEO calls it “early”).
  • 2027 – Planned testing of background AI models for order entry.
  • Future – Potential rollout of personalized digital menus after testing; exact launch date not disclosed.

💡 Why it matters

  • Enhances individual customer experience at high‑traffic drive‑thrus.
  • Aims to reduce order errors and speed up service.
  • Extends AI use beyond internal tools to visible consumer‑facing interfaces.
  • Signals broader industry interest in AI‑driven personalization (as seen at Taco Bell and McDonald’s).

#Starbucks #AI #DriveThru #Personalization

Source: Starbucks wants to use AI to show you a ‘personalized digital menu’ at the drive-thru

item.title: AWS Amazon Connect Customer Named Leader in 2026 Gartner CCaaS Magic Quadrant
item.description:
AWS Amazon Connect Customer Named Leader in 2026 Gartner CCaaS Magic Quadrant

Amazon Web Services (AWS) has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) for Amazon Connect for the fourth consecutive year.

📊 Recognition

  • “I’m proud to share that Amazon Web Services (AWS) has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) for Amazon Connect for the fourth consecutive year.”
  • “I’m proud of the Connect Customer team for receiving this recognition for the fourth year in a row.”
  • “Read the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service: Gartner, Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service, 19 October 2026, Drew Kraus Et Al.”
  • “Gartner does not endorse any company, vendor, product or service depicted in its publications….”

🧩 How it works

  • “When we launched Amazon Connect Customer, we set out to evolve how businesses serve their customers: to make personalized, intelligent experiences possible without giving up efficiency, flexibility, or control.”
  • “Connect Customer builds a living picture of every customer: who they are, what they’ve been through, what they need next.”
  • “Every touchpoint draws on that intelligence.”
  • “Meeting that takes more than traditional contact center technology, it takes a comprehensive solution that brings together customer context, AI, and the flexibility to adapt.”

⚙️ Key capabilities

  • “Most of the industry is still optimizing for deflection: getting customers away from humans as fast as possible.”
  • “We took a different path.”
  • “Connect Customer is built for the hard things: the disputed claim, the renegotiated mortgage, the disrupted itinerary that needs real action and can’t go wrong.”
  • “We carry those interactions all the way through to resolution, and we make them feel natural and personal.”
  • “Generative and agentic AI push this further: understanding what a customer needs and acting on it.”
  • “Every action is auditable.”
  • “Humans step in when the moment calls for it.”
  • “You get enterprise scale and the confidence that nothing slips through the cracks.”

💡 Why it matters

  • “People expect you to recognize them, understand what they need, and stay consistent across every channel.”
  • “They don’t want to repeat themselves.”
  • “They don’t want to navigate disconnected systems to solve a simple problem.”
  • “They want interactions that feel natural, relevant, and genuinely helpful.”
  • “The companies that win the next decade of customer experience won’t be the ones with the most channels or the fastest bot.”
  • “Connect Customer exists to make that real for businesses of every size.”
  • “Our engineers, product teams, partners, and customers shaped what we’ve built.”

The Gartner document is available upon request from AWS.

#AWS #ContactCenter #AI

Source: AWS named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contact Center as a Service | Amazon Web Services

item.title: AI Hallucinations Undermine Customer Service Workers' Authority
item.description:
AI Hallucinations Undermine Customer Service Workers’ Authority

Generative AI tools are increasingly causing customers to challenge the expertise of service workers, leading to dangerous situations like ignored allergy warnings and dismissed sommeliers.

🔍 Overview

A growing number of customer service workers report that patrons are trusting AI-generated information over the advice of human experts, a trend exacerbated by AI hallucinations. This phenomenon is affecting restaurants, national parks, childcare facilities, and other service industries.

🧩 How it works

Customers use generative AI tools like ChatGPT to answer questions or plan experiences. When the AI produces incorrect information — known as a hallucination — some users insist the AI is correct, even when confronted by human professionals.

Examples from the evidence include:

  • A server in New York City, Madison, has guests push back when she tells them a dish contains an allergen, saying “ChatGPT disagrees.”
  • One diner with a shellfish allergy ordered a fish dish with a shellfish-based broth because they believed ChatGPT over the server’s warning.
  • Sommeliers at a Michelin-recommended Italian restaurant are being dismissed from tables as guests prefer to ask ChatGPT for wine recommendations.
  • Customers have requested bottles that the restaurant doesn’t carry — or that don’t exist at all.

⚙️ Key details

The issue extends well beyond restaurants:

  • River rangers: Jason, a river ranger on federal lands in the Mountain West, says visitors arrive with nonsensical AI-generated itineraries that include hallucinated campsites or schedules out of geographical order. Some groups remain skeptical even when rangers explain the errors while pointing at a map.
  • Childcare professionals: Casey, an after-school program teacher in New York, reports parents and caretakers turning to ChatGPT or Claude for childhood development advice. One family insisted that ChatGPT’s recommended sleep schedule was fine, even though the child needed two to three more hours of sleep a night based on his behavior.
  • General customer service: Workers at movie theaters, coffee shops, and Apple Stores report customers asking for products or features that don’t exist.

💡 Why it matters

“Mass adoption of generative AI tools is rewriting the old adage that has long been a thorn in the side of restaurant and retail workers: ‘The customer is always right,’” according to the evidence. Now, workers must contend with customers who trust AI chatbots over human expertise.

To “soften the blow” of AI hallucinations, Madison and her colleagues soften their language, saying things like, “We have this really hyper-specific wine list, maybe it’s showing you a French wine, and we don’t carry French wine,” instead of telling the customer the AI made up a wine brand.

The launch of a new AI agent, Muse from Meta, is expected to worsen the problem, as are similar tools from other companies.
